events.name: Marilyn Monroe: A Portrait
events.style: Centenary retrospective in portraits, not film stills
events.whyGo: Monroe's centenary, told entirely through portraiture rather than the usual film stills. Closes in under two weeks.
events.opNote: Off-peak Monday to Thursday is £25-£27; weekends £27-£30.

events.name: M.C. Escher. The Exhibition
events.style: Major survey of Escher's prints
events.whyGo: A year into its run and closing within two weeks - the last chance at a major Escher show for years. The Embankment Galleries give the tessellations real wall space.
events.opNote: Timed entry; the final weekends will be busiest.

events.name: Cecily Brown: Picture Making
events.style: New paintings made for the park setting
events.whyGo: Free, painted in response to the gallery's park setting, and one of the best reasons to fold a gallery stop into a Hyde Park walk this year.
events.opNote: Closes 6 September. The processing... display in the education space closes the same day.

events.name: Project a Black Planet: The Art and Culture of Panafrica
events.style: A century of Pan-African art and print culture, 250+ works
events.whyGo: Paintings, film, journals and posters tracing Pan-Africanism from the 1920s on - a century of visual culture that rarely gets a London show at this scale. Closes early September.
events.opNote: Price not published on the listing page - check barbican.org.uk when booking.

events.name: The Great River Race
events.style: 300 traditional boats racing 21.6 miles through all of London's bridges
events.typicalWhen: The second Saturday in September
events.address: Start at Millwall, finish at Ham
events.duration: An hour or so at any one bridge
events.whyGo: Gigs, skiffs, dragon boats and Celtic longboats - about 300 of them, from serious clubs to fancy-dress novelty crews - race under all 28 bridges between the Docklands and Richmond. The best day of the year to lean on a bridge and watch the river.
events.opNote: Free from any bridge or bank on the route. It runs upstream with the tide, so check the start time to work out when it reaches your stretch.

events.name: Grease: The Immersive Movie Musical
events.style: Live musical staged around the audience
events.whyGo: The film staged as a live musical with the audience inside the set rather than in front of it, in a purpose-built venue in Battersea Park.
events.opNote: CLOSES 13 SEPTEMBER 2026 - a short run, and the nearest thing on this list to already being over.

events.name: Photo Portrait Now 2026
events.style: New photographic portraiture from six universities
events.whyGo: Free, and a read on where photographic portraiture is heading - judged new-graduate work rather than established names.
events.opNote: Combine with the ticketed Monroe show while both run.

events.name: Early Netherlandish Drawings
events.style: 15th and 16th-century works on paper
events.whyGo: Free, final weeks, and a genre the museum rarely gives a dedicated room. Pair with the free Constable show in the same building.
events.opNote: No ticket needed; walk in with general admission.

events.name: Tools for Transition and Mineral
events.style: Two free Design Museum research displays, closing together
events.whyGo: Two free displays on one floor - design responses to housing and resource pressure, and UK geology's role in the green transition - closing the same day, so one visit covers both.
events.opNote: Both on Level 2; the ticketed NIGO show is separate.

events.name: Open House Festival
events.style: 800+ normally closed buildings open free across every borough
events.typicalWhen: A week to ten days in mid-September
events.duration: As many buildings as you can fit
events.whyGo: The one week a year you can walk into the Lloyd's Building, private livery halls and architects' own homes for nothing. The 2026 programme marks the Lloyd's Building's 40th birthday.
events.opNote: Most buildings are walk-in but the famous ones are ticketed ballots that open weeks ahead and fill within hours - plan those first. 2026 booking opened 19 August.

events.name: London Design Festival
events.style: City-wide design festival across eleven design districts
events.venue: Design districts city-wide, plus the V&A and Design Museum
events.typicalWhen: Mid-to-late September, the same week as Open House
events.address: Districts include Bankside, Brompton, Shoreditch and Chelsea
events.whyGo: Eleven design districts run trails, installations and open studios, with the V&A and Design Museum programming their own strands rather than hosting incidentally. It rewards picking one neighbourhood over trying to see all of it.
events.opNote: Runs the same week as Open House London, so architecture and design combine into one dense week. Talks and forums book up; the district trails are walk-in.

events.name: Lasting Impressions: Women Printmakers 1900-Now
events.style: A century of printmaking by women
events.whyGo: Free, easy to miss inside a museum this size, and a rare thematic thread - women printmakers specifically - rather than a general survey.
events.opNote: A display within the free museum; no ticket.

events.name: James McNeill Whistler
events.style: Full Whistler retrospective
events.whyGo: Whistler gets a full retrospective far less often than his Impressionist contemporaries, and this one closes at the end of September.
events.opNote: Free for Tate Members. Price not on the listing page - check when booking.

events.name: LUMINISCENCE
events.style: 360-degree projection concert in a cathedral
events.whyGo: Projection mapped across the inside of Westminster Cathedral with live music - the unfinished blackened brick above the marble takes the light unusually well.
events.opNote: In the cathedral itself, which is otherwise free to enter. Closes 27 September 2026.

events.name: Totally Thames
events.style: A month of river-themed events across twenty boroughs
events.venue: Along the Thames, Richmond to Barking
events.typicalWhen: The whole of September
events.whyGo: Over a hundred river events under one umbrella - foreshore walks, boat festivals, art installations - that absorbed the old Mayor's Thames Festival. A September visit can be built around it without realising it is one programme.
events.opNote: Most events free and unticketed. Highlights in 2026 include Chiswick Tidefest on 6 September and the St Katharine Docks Classic Boat Festival on 12-13 September.

events.name: NIGO: From Japan with Love
events.style: Retrospective of the streetwear designer
events.whyGo: A rare institutional show for a streetwear figure rather than a traditional designer - BAPE, Human Made and two decades of Japanese street culture.
events.opNote: Closes early October. Price not on the listing - check when booking.

events.name: John Constable: Views of Nature
events.style: Constable's works on paper
events.whyGo: Free, and focused on the drawings and watercolours rather than the oils everyone knows from the National Gallery.
events.opNote: Walk in with general admission.

events.name: The National Portrait Gallery's Portrait Award 2026
events.style: The annual contemporary portrait painting prize
events.whyGo: Free, judged rather than curated, and the quickest way to see where contemporary portrait painting actually is this year. Usually quieter than the ticketed shows downstairs.
events.opNote: On Floor 2, away from the Monroe queues.

events.name: Anish Kapoor
events.style: Major survey anchoring the Southbank Centre's 75th year
events.whyGo: The anchor show of the Southbank Centre's 75th anniversary, and Kapoor's large-scale work suits the Hayward's raw concrete unusually well.
events.opNote: The smaller Jen Liu show runs alongside in the same building to the same closing date.

events.name: BFI London Film Festival
events.style: The UK's biggest public film festival
events.venue: BFI Southbank and cinemas across the West End
events.typicalWhen: Twelve days in October
events.whyGo: Unlike Cannes or Venice, anyone can buy a ticket to the premieres - no accreditation, just booking speed. The 2026 edition is the 70th.
events.opNote: Public booking opens in September and the galas go fast; ordinary screenings of the same films are far easier to get.

events.name: Serpentine Pavilion 2026
events.style: This year's architecture commission, by LANZA atelier
events.whyGo: Each year's Pavilion is demolished at the end of October and never rebuilt - see it or miss it permanently. Free, outdoors, and a natural stop on a Kensington Gardens walk.
events.opNote: The Soto walk-through sculpture nearby closes the same day, so the two make one outdoor stop.

events.name: Jesus Rafael Soto: Penetrable BBL Jaune
events.style: A kinetic sculpture you walk through
events.whyGo: Physically walk-through rather than look-at - hanging yellow strands you push into and disappear inside - which makes it the most child-friendly thing on the autumn art calendar.
events.opNote: Outdoors by Serpentine South; closes with the Pavilion on 25 October.

events.name: Diwali on the Square
events.style: The Mayor of London's free Diwali festival
events.typicalWhen: A Sunday in October or November, moving with the Hindu lunar calendar
events.whyGo: London's biggest single Diwali gathering, around 35,000 people, with the Mayor lighting the ceremonial lamp. City-hall-run and completely free, like Eid and Vaisakhi on the same square.
events.opNote: 2026 edition confirmed for Sunday 25 October, 1pm-7pm. No ticket, just turn up.

events.name: A National Portrait
events.style: A crowd-built digital portrait with Es Devlin
events.whyGo: Visitors contribute to the work rather than only viewing it - a collective national portrait built with Es Devlin, who designed the London 2012 closing ceremony staging.
events.opNote: Free; drop in around the ticketed shows.

events.name: Frieze London and Frieze Sculpture
events.style: Contemporary art fair, with a free outdoor sculpture park alongside
events.typicalWhen: The fair is five days in mid-October; the free sculpture runs mid-September to the start of November
events.duration: An hour for the sculpture, half a day for the fair
events.price: Sculpture free; fair day tickets roughly £50-£65
events.whyGo: The ticketed fair gets the coverage, but Frieze Sculpture is the half guides miss - six weeks of large-scale outdoor work in the English Gardens, free, no ticket. The fair itself runs 15-18 October 2026.
events.opNote: Dates span the free sculpture run; the fair is 14 October (invitation preview) then public 15-18 October. Fair pricing unverified for 2026 - check before quoting.

events.name: Mundo Pixar Experience
events.style: Walk-through recreations of fourteen Pixar films
events.whyGo: Fourteen Pixar worlds rebuilt at full size across 3,500 square metres - Andy's room from Toy Story at toy scale, the Monsters, Inc. scare floor, Flo's café from Cars. The London run has a room built for it that no other city got.
events.opNote: Closes 1 November 2026 and the organisers say it does not return afterwards. Wembley Park station, then a short walk past the stadium.

events.name: Schiaparelli: Fashion Becomes Art
events.style: The couture house's surrealist work as art objects
events.whyGo: The V&A's headline fashion show of the year, treating Schiaparelli's Dali-era surrealism as art rather than garments on mannequins. Book ahead - it will not have walk-up availability.
events.opNote: Weekday tickets £2 cheaper. Closes 8 November.

events.name: The Traitors: Live Experience
events.style: Playable version of the TV format
events.whyGo: You sit at the Round Table, you are secretly assigned Faithful or Traitor, and you have to lie to a room of strangers for an hour and a half.
events.opNote: Booked as an individual rather than a group, so you play with strangers unless you buy out a sitting - which is the point of the format.

events.name: The Lord Mayor's Show
events.style: A procession that has run since 1215
events.typicalWhen: The second Saturday in November
events.address: Mansion House to the Royal Courts of Justice
events.duration: A morning, with fireworks at dusk
events.whyGo: A procession that has run every year since 1215 - state coach, livery companies, floats and a river of marching bands through the Square Mile, followed by fireworks on the Thames.
events.opNote: Free and one of the oldest civic events in the world. Get a spot on Cheapside or Fleet Street early; the fireworks are from the river at dusk.

events.name: Inside Aardman: Wallace & Gromit and Friends
events.style: The stop-motion studio's craft, for children
events.whyGo: How Aardman actually makes the films - plasticine, sets and rigs - at the children's V&A in Bethnal Green. A different show from the Battersea Wallace & Gromit experience, and better for younger children.
events.opNote: Distinct from Larger Than Life at Battersea - do not confuse the two when booking.

events.name: Winston Churchill: The Painter
events.style: A major retrospective of Churchill's paintings
events.whyGo: The side of Churchill almost nobody associates with him, in a townhouse museum that rarely runs ticketed shows at all.
events.opNote: The permanent Wallace Collection around it stays free.

events.name: Declaring Independence: USA 250
events.style: 250 years of American independence through the museum's collections
events.whyGo: Free and timed to the US semiquincentennial - a different angle for American visitors than the museum's ancient-world halls.
events.opNote: Pairs with the ticketed Bayeux Tapestry loan in the same building from September.

events.name: The Waldorf Project: Chapter Five / KAIHOGYO
events.style: Long-form sensory art
events.whyGo: A sustained sensory work rather than a show with a running time - the Waldorf Project's chapters are closer to endurance art than theatre.
events.opNote: Runs 19 November to 20 December 2026. Over-18, and demanding by design - not a casual evening out.

events.name: The Peter Pan Cup
events.style: The Serpentine club's Christmas morning race in an unheated lake
events.typicalWhen: Christmas morning, every year since 1864
events.whyGo: Serpentine Swimming Club members race across open cold water on Christmas morning while the rest of the park watches in coats - named for the Peter Pan statue nearby and run since 1864. One of the only things happening in London on the day itself.
events.opNote: Spectating is free and unticketed; swimming is members-only with qualifying swims through the winter. Mid-morning by the Lido.

events.name: London New Year's Eve Fireworks
events.style: The midnight fireworks fired from the London Eye - ticketed, not walk-up
events.venue: The Thames between Westminster and the Eye
events.typicalWhen: Midnight, 31 December
events.whyGo: The most important fact is operational: since 2014 this has NOT been a free walk-up event. The riverside is gated and ticketed, tickets sell out months ahead, and a guide that skips this sends readers to be turned away at midnight.
events.opNote: Tickets released via london.gov.uk months in advance. Without one, the fireworks are visible poorly or not at all from outside the zones - Primrose Hill and other high ground are the unticketed alternatives.

events.name: Concrete and Clay: Archiving the Barbican
events.style: The estate's own architectural history, free
events.whyGo: The Brutalist estate explaining itself - the best primer before wandering the highwalks, and it closes for good on New Year's Day 2027 despite feeling permanent.
events.opNote: Free, inside the Centre; combine with the conservatory's Sunday openings.

events.name: London New Year's Day Parade
events.style: 8,000 performers parade Piccadilly to Parliament Square every 1 January
events.typicalWhen: 1 January, every year, whatever the weather
events.address: Route from Piccadilly to Parliament Square
events.price: Free from the route; grandstands paid
events.whyGo: Around 8,000 performers - marching bands, cheerleaders, floats - walk the same 2.2-mile route every New Year's Day. One of the only major London events guaranteed to a fixed date you can build a trip around.
events.opNote: Free along the whole route; paid grandstand seats exist near Piccadilly. Starts around midday.

events.name: Hampton Court Palace Ice Rink
events.style: Skating against the Tudor palace facade
events.typicalWhen: Late November to the first weekend of January
events.whyGo: The most atmospheric rink in the London area for the Tudor backdrop alone, with adults-only evening sessions on selected dates. Christmas weekends sell out.
events.opNote: Dates from listings sites, not yet confirmed on the rink's own site - check before booking travel.

events.name: Frida: The Making of an Icon
events.style: How Kahlo's public image was constructed
events.whyGo: Framed around Kahlo's image-making rather than straight biography - a different show from the Kahlo retrospectives most people have already seen.
events.opNote: Runs through the Christmas peak; book the quiet January weekdays.

events.name: Peaky Blinders: Underworld
events.style: Walk-through Shelby underworld
events.whyGo: Starts in a rebuilt Garrison Tavern, then a hidden door drops you into the Shelby underworld to wander, meet actors and work things out for yourself.
events.opNote: In the railway arches at 8 Bermondsey Street - the aggregator files it under London Bridge, which sends people to the wrong side of the station.

events.name: Hyde Park Winter Wonderland
events.style: Christmas market, rides and ice rink
events.typicalWhen: Mid-November to early January
events.price: Free entry off-peak, timed ticket at peak
events.whyGo: A hundred and fifty-odd rides, bars and market stalls across Hyde Park, plus the largest outdoor ice rink in the city - the biggest Christmas thing London does.
events.opNote: Entry is free at quiet times and ticketed at peak, but the RIDES AND RINK ARE PAID SEPARATELY and it adds up fast. Weekday afternoons are the only calm slots.

events.name: Leicester Square Christmas Market
events.style: Bavarian-style chalets in the West End
events.typicalWhen: Early November to just after New Year
events.whyGo: The central, no-ticket Christmas market, running the whole festive period. The chalet bar packages are the only ticketed part - the market itself costs nothing to enter.
events.opNote: Bar packages from about £26.50 book separately. Rammed on December weekends.

events.name: Southbank Centre Winter Market
events.style: Free-entry riverside Christmas market
events.typicalWhen: Mid-November to just after Christmas
events.whyGo: The free-entry alternative to ticketed Winter Wonderland - chalets, food and mulled wine along the river with the Eye behind, walkable as part of a South Bank evening rather than an outing in itself.
events.opNote: No entry fee; you pay at the stalls. Busiest weekend evenings.

events.name: Natural History Museum Ice Rink
events.style: The rink in front of the Waterhouse terracotta facade
events.typicalWhen: Late October to early January
events.whyGo: The most photographed rink in London, for the museum facade behind the ice. Returned in 2023 after a two-year gap and has run each winter since.
events.opNote: IMPORTANT: dates and prices here come from resellers - the museum's own site would not respond when checked. Verify at nhm.ac.uk before publishing dates anywhere else.

events.name: Skate at Somerset House
events.style: The courtyard rink with the 40ft tree
events.typicalWhen: Mid-November to mid-January
events.whyGo: The most elegant of the central rinks - a working arts venue's courtyard rather than a fenced-off park - with late adult sessions alongside family daytimes.
events.opNote: Skate Lates evenings run DJ sessions; daytime is family territory. Book a slot type deliberately.

events.name: Justin Caguiat: Change Ringing
events.style: First UK institutional show for the painter
events.whyGo: A first UK institutional show spanning painting, sculpture, print, sound and film - genuine discovery rather than greatest hits, and free.
events.opNote: Amar Kanwar runs at Serpentine North across the bridge; one visit covers both.

events.name: The Music Is Black: A British Story
events.style: The history of Black British music, at the new V&A East
events.address: Stratford Waterfront, Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park
events.whyGo: A flagship show at the brand-new V&A East, telling a specifically British story rather than importing an American music history.
events.opNote: V&A East is at Stratford, not South Kensington - a different building entirely.

events.name: Rising Voices: Contemporary Art from Asia, Australia and the Pacific
events.style: A broad regional survey
events.whyGo: Asia, Australia and the Pacific in one survey - broader than the V&A usually attempts, and £11 cheaper than its Schiaparelli headliner.
events.opNote: Works as the second show on a Schiaparelli visit.

events.name: Sophie's Surprise Christmas Party
events.style: Circus and comedy Christmas show
events.typicalWhen: Mid-November to early January
events.whyGo: Circus, cabaret and comedy in a Christmas show that is emphatically not for children, and returns most years.
events.opNote: Runs 13 November 2026 to 10 January 2027. Over-18 - the name is misleading and families do turn up expecting otherwise.

events.name: Ana Mendieta
events.style: Survey of the Cuban-American performance and land artist
events.whyGo: Mendieta's body-and-land work rarely gets a full London survey. Some pieces deal with violence against women - not a casual outing, and worth knowing before booking.
events.opNote: Content warnings apply; check Tate's guidance.

events.name: Zineb Sedira: When Words Fall Silent, Cinema Speaks
events.style: The Tate Britain Commission, filling the Duveen Galleries
events.whyGo: Free, and the annual Commission uses the Duveen Galleries at a scale no room-based show can. Sedira represented France at the Venice Biennale.
events.opNote: In the free central galleries - no ticket.

events.name: Yuko Mohri: In Concert
events.style: Kinetic sound work built for the Barbican's Curve
events.whyGo: Built specifically for the Curve's shape by an artist who represented Japan at Venice - site-responsive in the literal sense.
events.opNote: Price not on the listing - check when booking.

events.name: Korea
events.style: Major loan exhibition of Korean art and history
events.whyGo: Korean art at a scale London rarely sees, overlapping the Bayeux Tapestry in the same building for four months - book both for one visit.
events.opNote: Price not yet published - check when booking opens.

events.name: Painting the French Riviera
events.style: Picasso, Matisse and the Cote d'Azur, 1870s-1960s
events.whyGo: Over 160 works - Picasso, Matisse, Cezanne, Renoir - organised with the Cleveland Museum of Art, so this exact loan list will not reassemble.
events.opNote: RA Friends preview 29 September to 1 October; free for Friends throughout.

events.name: Amar Kanwar
events.style: Meditative film installation
events.duration: An hour if you let it work
events.whyGo: Free and built to be sat with rather than lapped - the counterweight to a day of blockbuster queues.
events.opNote: Across the bridge from the Caguiat show; one visit covers both galleries.

events.name: Renoir and Love
events.style: The biggest UK Renoir show in twenty years
events.whyGo: The most significant UK Renoir exhibition in two decades - weekends and holiday dates will sell out, so book rather than stroll up.
events.opNote: Selected Friday evenings run pay-what-you-wish entry. Overlaps Van Eyck in the same building from late November.

events.name: PLATFORM: Simone Brewster
events.style: One designer's practice, free
events.whyGo: The museum's free PLATFORM slot, given to a single contemporary designer - a lower-commitment stop than the ticketed shows upstairs.
events.opNote: Museum publishes the close only as January 2027; the exact day here is provisional.

events.name: Club NVRLND
events.style: Peter Pan as a nightclub musical
events.whyGo: Peter Pan rewritten as a club night, with the cast performing around a dancefloor you are standing on rather than a stage you face.
events.opNote: Runs 14 November 2026 to 31 January 2027. Over-18.

events.name: Tim Walker's Fairyland: Love and Legends
events.style: Fashion photography turned to queer identity and legend
events.whyGo: One of Britain's best-known fashion photographers working well outside his editorial register - queer identity, community and legend rather than campaigns.
events.opNote: Tickets were not yet on sale when checked - watch npg.org.uk near the October opening.

events.name: Chinese New Year in London
events.style: Europe's largest Lunar New Year celebration - parade, lions, Chinatown shut to traffic
events.venue: Trafalgar Square, Shaftesbury Avenue and Chinatown
events.typicalWhen: The Sunday closest to Lunar New Year, late January to mid-February
events.whyGo: Europe's largest gathering of Chinese lions and dragons parades from Trafalgar Square into a Chinatown closed to traffic for the day. Several hundred thousand people come, so arrive well before the late-morning start.
events.opNote: Lunar New Year 2027 falls Saturday 6 February; London celebrates the following day. Full programme publishes nearer the time.

events.name: The 90s: Art and Fashion
events.style: YBA-era art and 90s British fashion together
events.whyGo: The YBAs and 90s British fashion in one show - a wider lens than the single-medium retrospectives, running through Valentine's week and half term.
events.opNote: Free for Tate Members; price otherwise unpublished when checked.

events.name: Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography
events.style: Photography's first claim to be art
events.whyGo: Free, and reaches back to photography's earliest art claims - an unusual historical register for Tate Modern, and no ticket alongside the paid shows.
events.opNote: Pairs with any ticketed show on the same visit.

events.name: London Fashion Week
events.style: The shows are closed; the public fringe is the visitable part
events.typicalWhen: Five days in mid-September and five in mid-to-late February
events.price: Public events free to ticketed; runway shows invitation-only
events.whyGo: Unlike Paris or Milan, London runs a genuine public fringe - designer pop-up sales and British Fashion Council exhibitions alongside the closed shows - so a visitor without an invitation still has something real to do beyond people-watching outside venues.
events.opNote: February 2027 edition confirmed 19-23 February. The public programme publishes at londonfashionweek.co.uk close to each edition.

events.name: Robert Ryman: The Real Thing
events.style: The white-on-white paintings, in full retrospective
events.whyGo: Ryman's white monochromes divide people like little else in modern painting - a full retrospective is the honest way to decide for yourself.
events.opNote: Fills the whole main gallery; allow longer than a single-room show.

events.name: Nan Goldin: You Never Did Anything Wrong
events.style: Full retrospective of the photographer
events.whyGo: One of the most significant living photographers in full retrospective - addiction, intimacy and the AIDS crisis, and genuinely not family viewing, which is worth knowing before booking.
events.opNote: Dates from the Southbank Centre's own announcement; price and formal age guidance unconfirmed.

events.name: Gathering Ground
events.style: Free group show
events.whyGo: Free with a long run into March - the reliable wet-weather fallback at Tate Modern whatever else is on.
events.opNote: No booking pressure; walk in.

events.name: Peggy Guggenheim in London: The Making of a Collector
events.style: How the collection was actually built
events.whyGo: The collector's story rather than the collection's greatest hits - the right show for anyone who has already done the Venice museum.
events.opNote: Runs the whole winter; overlaps French Riviera in the same building through January.

events.name: Vanessa Bell & Duncan Grant: Inside Bloomsbury
events.style: The Bloomsbury Group's two central painters
events.whyGo: Bell and Grant carried the Bloomsbury Group's visual side, and the run spans Christmas to spring - a natural tie-in with our Bloomsbury guide.
events.opNote: Free for Tate Members.

events.name: Van Eyck: The Portraits
events.style: The first exhibition ever devoted to Van Eyck's portraiture
events.whyGo: The first show ever devoted to Van Eyck's portraits - an unrepeatable claim, not marketing. Overlaps Renoir in the same building for two months.
events.opNote: Book well ahead for December-January dates.

events.name: Tarek Atoui: Hyundai Commission
events.style: The Turbine Hall commission, built from sound
events.whyGo: The Turbine Hall commission is always free and always at a scale nothing else in London matches - this year's is built around sound.
events.opNote: Walk in; the hall is the museum's front door.

events.name: Secret Cinema Presents Pirates of the Caribbean
events.style: Film screening inside a built world
events.whyGo: Secret Cinema's format: a full set built around the film, actors in it, and you in costume before the screening starts.
events.opNote: 16 February to 25 April 2027 - the furthest ahead on this list. Costume is expected rather than optional.

events.name: London Coffee Festival
events.style: Four days of coffee, tastings and barista competition at the Truman Brewery
events.typicalWhen: Four days in mid-May - trade days first, public weekend after
events.whyGo: About 275 coffee and food brands fill the old brewery, with the Coffee Masters competition running through the trade days. A reliable preview of what turns up in London's actual cafes over the following year.
events.opNote: 13-16 May 2027 confirmed on the festival's own site; tickets not yet on sale at the time of checking.

events.name: Monet: Painting Time
events.style: A major Monet retrospective on light and time
events.whyGo: Monet blockbusters sell out months ahead and readers plan trips around them - flagged now even though it opens in February 2027.
events.opNote: Booking will open well before the February opening; free for Tate Members.

events.name: The Bayeux Tapestry
events.style: The Tapestry's first time out of France in nearly a millennium
events.whyGo: The actual Bayeux Tapestry, leaving France for the first time in nearly a thousand years. The single biggest cultural loan London has hosted in decades, and the one exhibition this year to plan a trip around.
events.opNote: Opens 10 September 2026 and runs to July 2027. Expect the tightest booking of anything on this page.

events.name: Doggett's Coat and Badge Race
events.style: The oldest continuously held annual sporting event in the world
events.venue: The Thames, London Bridge to Cadogan Pier
events.typicalWhen: One afternoon in late summer - the month has drifted between July and September, so check
events.duration: About half an hour to pass any one point
events.whyGo: Single scullers race four miles and seven furlongs from London Bridge to Chelsea for a scarlet coat and silver badge, as they have since 1715 - older than the Boat Race and the Derby. Watch free from any bridge on the route.
events.opNote: The 312th running starts 1.15pm on 2 September 2026. Organised by the Fishmongers' and Watermen's Companies, who have never needed to market it - which is why almost nobody watching knows what they are seeing.

events.name: Eid on the Square
events.style: The Mayor of London's free Eid al-Adha festival
events.typicalWhen: Moves with the Islamic lunar calendar, roughly eleven days earlier each year - it fell on 30 May in 2026
events.whyGo: Twenty years running, and deliberately plural - Turkish, Middle Eastern, Malaysian, Indonesian, North African and South Asian communities share one stage rather than a single homogenous Eid. BSL interpretation and access are built in.
events.opNote: The 2026 edition ran 30 May. The 2027 date will fall roughly eleven days earlier and is not yet published - do not guess it.

events.name: Trooping the Colour
events.style: The King's official birthday parade - massed bands, cavalry, RAF flypast
events.venue: Horse Guards Parade and The Mall
events.typicalWhen: A Saturday in mid-June, with full dress rehearsals the two Saturdays before
events.price: Free from The Mall; stand seats by ballot
events.whyGo: The parade everyone knows - the useful detail is the two rehearsals on the preceding Saturdays. The Major General's Review and the Colonel's Review are near-identical dress rehearsals with a fraction of the crowd.
events.opNote: 2026 ran 13 June with rehearsals 30 May and 6 June. 2027 date not yet announced; the mid-June Saturday pattern holds.

events.name: Royal Gun Salutes
events.style: The King's Troop gallops six guns across Hyde Park and fires a 41-gun salute
events.venue: Hyde Park or Green Park, and the Tower of London
events.typicalWhen: Fixed royal dates every year: 6 May, the King's official birthday in June, 8 September and 14 November, plus state occasions
events.whyGo: Horse-drawn guns arrive at the gallop, fire blank rounds at ten-second intervals, and leave - dramatic, free, and unknown to most visitors because it is never marketed as an event. The Tower fires 62 rounds the same day.
events.opNote: Recurs on the same handful of dates every year, which makes it one of the easiest free spectacles to plan around. Hyde Park salutes usually fire at noon - check royal.uk for each date.

events.name: The Knollys Rose Ceremony
events.style: One red rose, carried in procession, paid to the Lord Mayor as 645-year-old rent
events.venue: Seething Lane garden to Mansion House
events.typicalWhen: Around 24 June, a weekday
events.whyGo: Sir Robert Knolles built a footbridge without permission in 1381 and the fine - one red rose a year - is still being paid, in person, in procession. Revived in 1924 and performed to almost no audience at all.
events.opNote: A weekday in late June, unticketed and barely publicised. Check the Company of Watermen or City events listings for the exact date.

events.name: Pearly Kings and Queens Harvest Festival
events.style: The Pearlies in full button suits - procession, maypole and a harvest church service
events.typicalWhen: A Sunday in late September, from early afternoon
events.whyGo: Thousands of hand-sewn buttons, 150 years of costermonger tradition, morris dancing in Guildhall Yard and a working church service at St Mary-le-Bow. As visually distinctive as Carnival with a fraction of the attention.
events.opNote: 2025 ran Sunday 21 September from 1.15pm; the 2026 date follows the same late-September Sunday pattern but was unconfirmed when checked.

events.name: St Patrick's Day Parade and Festival
events.style: Free Irish parade to a Trafalgar Square stage festival
events.venue: Hyde Park Corner to Trafalgar Square
events.typicalWhen: The Sunday closest to 17 March
events.whyGo: More than 50,000 people watch bands from the UK, Ireland and the US process a mile and a half to a full afternoon of live Irish music in Trafalgar Square. Mayor-produced, so free start to finish.
events.opNote: 2027's parade should fall Sunday 14 March by the usual pattern - unconfirmed until London.gov publishes it.

events.name: The Boat Race
events.style: Oxford v Cambridge on the Championship Course, free from the bank
events.typicalWhen: A Saturday in late March or early April - the date follows the tides
events.duration: The race passes in minutes; the day is an afternoon
events.whyGo: The crowded spots are Putney at the start and Hammersmith Bridge; Barnes Bridge near the finish is far less mobbed and the race is usually still alive there. Free the whole four and a quarter miles.
events.opNote: Exact date announced each year once tides are known. The towpath pubs fill hours ahead.

events.name: Head of the River Race
events.style: 400+ eights race the Boat Race course in procession
events.typicalWhen: A Saturday in mid-to-late March, usually just before the Boat Race
events.whyGo: The same stretch of river as the Boat Race but with several hundred crews instead of two - a far better spectacle for anyone who wants to watch rowing rather than a rivalry. Nothing to book because there is nothing to buy.
events.opNote: Run with the ebb tide, Mortlake down to Putney. Any towpath spot works.

events.name: The Championships, Wimbledon
events.style: The Grand Slam, and The Queue is the walk-up route nobody believes exists
events.typicalWhen: Two weeks, late June into early July
events.price: Grounds passes from roughly £30; show courts by ballot
events.whyGo: The one genuinely useful fact: The Queue is a real same-day walk-up route to grounds tickets that needs no ballot - arrive early, queue on the grass, and you are in. Most first-time visitors have no idea it exists.
events.opNote: Show courts go by public ballot months ahead. The Queue starts the night before for the biggest days; a weekday-morning arrival usually gets a grounds pass.

events.name: All Points East
events.style: Two festival weekends in Victoria Park
events.typicalWhen: Two weekends across late August
events.whyGo: The east London festival that stayed put while Lovebox and Field Day moved on, now two full weekends. The 2026 second weekend was headlined by Lorde and Tyler, the Creator.
events.opNote: Single-day tickets per headliner rather than camping. 2027 dates announce around the new year.

events.name: BST Hyde Park
events.style: Stadium-scale single-day concerts in Hyde Park
events.typicalWhen: Headline Saturdays and Sundays from late June through mid-July
events.whyGo: One massive act per ticket, in central London, and back at your hotel by midnight - no tent, no fields. Lineups announce only a few months out, so it suits shorter-lead planning.
events.opNote: Between headline days the site runs Open House - free midweek entry to the arena with screens, bars and food. Worth knowing if you are in the park anyway.

events.name: Camden Fringe
events.style: 400+ fringe shows across small Camden venues every August
events.venue: Etcetera Theatre, Camden People's Theatre and a dozen more
events.typicalWhen: Four weeks across August
events.whyGo: The same density of new stand-up and theatre as Edinburgh every August, without the flight or the hotel prices - performers use it to preview the material they take north. Over 400 shows in 2025.
events.opNote: Programme publishes in early summer at camdenfringe.com. Most venues are pub theatres under 60 seats, so book the buzzy shows.

events.name: RHS Chelsea Flower Show
events.style: The world's most famous flower show, rebuilt from bare ground each May
events.typicalWhen: Five days in the third week of May - the first two are RHS members only
events.price: All tickets advance-only; roughly £30-£100+ by day
events.whyGo: An 11-acre site built from nothing every spring, shown for five days and dismantled within a week - about 157,000 people see it. Monday and Tuesday are members-only, which catches out anyone trying to book blind.
events.opNote: Book months ahead; the Friday and Saturday sell out first. The Sell-Off on the final afternoon, when exhibitors sell the actual plants, is the insider hour.

events.name: Meltdown
events.style: A festival programmed by a different guest artist every year
events.typicalWhen: Around ten days in June
events.whyGo: A single curator - Patti Smith, Grace Jones, Harry Styles in 2026 - books the whole festival, so the lineup is genuinely unpredictable rather than circuit-standard. The curator announcement itself is the news each spring.
events.opNote: Has skipped years before (2006, 2020-21), so confirm the current edition exists before planning around it.

events.name: Taste of London
events.style: London's restaurants serve taster menus in Regent's Park
events.typicalWhen: Five days in mid-to-late June
events.price: Entry from about £24, then pay per dish
events.whyGo: Dozens of real London restaurants serve small plates of their actual menus, so it works as a tasting flight of places you would otherwise book one by one. Friday sessions have historically had free children's entry.
events.opNote: Entry ticket plus pay-as-you-eat inside. 2025 ran 18-22 June; 2026-27 dates unverified when checked.

events.name: EFG London Jazz Festival
events.style: Ten days of jazz from the Barbican to pub back rooms
events.venue: Venues city-wide, anchored at the Southbank Centre
events.typicalWhen: About ten days in mid-November
events.price: Free fringe gigs up to £50+ headline concerts
events.whyGo: The same ten days span £60 Barbican headliners and £10 pub sessions, and the free fringe strand is the part visitor guides always skip. Programming runs across the small rooms in our live music guide.
events.opNote: Programme publishes around September at efglondonjazzfestival.org.uk. The famous names sell out; the discovery gigs do not.

events.name: Remembrance Sunday at the Cenotaph
events.style: The national act of remembrance, and the veterans' march-past after it
events.typicalWhen: The second Sunday in November, silence at 11am
events.duration: The morning, with the march-past continuing after
events.whyGo: The two-minute silence is the famous part; the veterans' march-past afterwards - thousands walking past the Cenotaph by association, for hours - is far less crowded to watch and at least as affecting.
events.opNote: Whitehall fills early for the ceremony itself. Arriving late morning for the march-past is the quieter way in.

events.name: Trafalgar Square Christmas Tree
events.style: Norway's annual thank-you gift, lit in early December with carols after
events.typicalWhen: Lighting ceremony in the first days of December; carols on the square most evenings until Christmas
events.whyGo: Norway has sent this tree every year since 1947 as thanks for wartime support - a real, continuous piece of diplomacy rather than decoration, usually lit by the Norwegian ambassador. Carol groups sing beneath it most December evenings, unticketed.
events.opNote: Tree up in late November, lit in the first week of December. The carols rota is published by Westminster council.

events.name: Jack in the Green, Deptford
events.style: A giant leaf-covered Jack paraded through Deptford with morris sides and drums
events.typicalWhen: May Day - 1 May or the nearest bank holiday weekend
events.whyGo: Fowlers Troop parade one of the tallest Jack in the Green figures in the country through streets no tourist visits, reviving a pagan May tradition that died out in Victorian London. No tickets, no marketing - you find it by knowing it exists.
events.opNote: Route and timing vary year to year and publish quietly. Deptford High Street mid-morning on the day is the safe bet.

events.name: London Mela
events.style: One of Europe's largest South Asian festivals, free in Gunnersbury Park
events.typicalWhen: A weekend in late August or early September
events.whyGo: Six-figure weekend attendance and barely a mention in mainstream round-ups - music, dance and food across one of Europe's biggest Melas. Gunnersbury Park and its museum are worth the trip on their own.
events.opNote: Free and unticketed. Check londonmela.org for the current year before travelling - the date moves within late summer.

events.name: West End Live
events.style: Casts of the current West End shows perform free in Trafalgar Square
events.typicalWhen: A weekend in mid-to-late June
events.whyGo: Full numbers from whatever is running in the West End, performed by the actual casts on an outdoor stage, for nothing. The programme is exactly as good as that year's theatre season.
events.opNote: Unticketed and rammed - the square reaches capacity by late morning, so go early to a specific show slot. Run by Westminster and the Society of London Theatre.

events.name: London Cocktail Week
events.style: One wristband, discounted signature cocktails at hundreds of bars
events.typicalWhen: Around ten days in early-to-mid October
events.duration: As many bars as you can manage
events.whyGo: The format is the draw: one wristband works at several hundred independent bars, which turns it into a self-guided crawl through neighbourhoods you would not otherwise hit in one trip. Pairs naturally with our cocktail bars guide.
events.opNote: Buy the wristband online ahead. Signature serves are discounted, not free.

events.name: Battle of Britain Anniversary Flypast
events.style: Historic RAF aircraft low over central London, free and barely publicised
events.venue: Over central London; service at Westminster Abbey
events.typicalWhen: The Sunday closest to 15 September
events.address: Best viewed from The Mall and Westminster
events.whyGo: A Spitfire and Hurricane from the Memorial Flight pass low over central London on the Sunday nearest the anniversary, with no publicity beyond RAF and Abbey channels. Most people who see it have no idea it happens every year.
events.opNote: Timing publishes quietly via the RAF; The Mall and the bridges give the clearest sightlines.

events.name: London Art Fair
events.style: A hundred galleries selling modern and contemporary art in Islington
events.typicalWhen: Mid-to-late January
events.whyGo: More than a hundred galleries fill the Business Design Centre in the dead week after New Year - a rare chance to buy directly from small dealers rather than watch an auction. January's most reliable indoor fixture.
events.opNote: Tickets cheaper online than on the door. Quietest on the weekday afternoons.

events.name: Shrove Tuesday Pancake Races
events.style: Fancy-dress relay races flipping pancakes, at several spots across town
events.typicalWhen: Shrove Tuesday - 47 days before Easter, February or early March
events.address: Old Spitalfields Market and other locations
events.whyGo: Teams in fancy dress flip pancakes down a marked course for a crowd of about a hundred - small, silly, and genuinely local rather than staged. The Spitalfields race is the reliable central one.
events.opNote: Shrove Tuesday 2027 falls on 9 February. Individual races publish quietly - check Old Spitalfields Market's events page.

events.name: Beating Retreat
events.style: Massed bands, cannon and drill at dusk on Horse Guards Parade
events.typicalWhen: Two evenings in June, just before Trooping the Colour
events.whyGo: The evening version of Trooping the Colour almost nobody outside London mentions - pipes, drums, cannon and cavalry at dusk, with a senior royal taking the salute. Ticketed, which keeps it far smaller than the parade itself.
events.opNote: Tickets via the Household Division; the two evenings differ slightly in programme.

events.name: Winter Lights
events.style: Free outdoor light-art trail
events.typicalWhen: Second half of January, nightly from about 5pm to 10pm
events.whyGo: Around twenty light installations by international artists, spread across the estate and the dockside after dark, free and with no ticket. The 2026 edition was the tenth.
events.opNote: No booking and no entry point - it is a self-guided trail across the whole estate, so arrive at any stop. Busiest at weekends; a weekday evening is much quieter.

events.name: Larger Than Life: Starring Wallace & Gromit
events.style: Aardman sets, models and animation
events.whyGo: Aardman's actual sets and models up close, where you can see the thumbprints left in the plasticine.
events.opNote: OPENS 14 OCTOBER 2026 - not open yet. No published closing date.

events.name: Phantom Peak
events.style: Open-world town you explore at your own pace
events.whyGo: A whole built town with more than twenty parallel storylines running at once - you pick which to follow and cannot see them all in one visit.
events.opNote: OPENS 4 DECEMBER 2026 at Westfield Stratford City. The original Canada Water venue CLOSED on 28 February 2026 after 625 performances - older guides still send people there.

events.name: Notting Hill Carnival
events.style: Europe's largest street carnival
events.typicalWhen: The August bank holiday weekend
events.whyGo: Two million people, Europe's biggest street carnival, led by London's Caribbean communities since 1966 - sound systems, mas bands and steel pan through the streets of W11, and free.
events.opNote: SUNDAY IS FAMILY DAY and much calmer than Monday. Ladbroke Grove and Westbourne Park stations go exit-only or shut entirely - plan the walk out before you go in.

events.name: The London Marathon
events.style: Mass-participation marathon through the city
events.typicalWhen: A Sunday in late April
events.whyGo: Free to watch and one of the great days in the London calendar - the start is on Blackheath, and the course runs through Greenwich, Tower Bridge and Canary Wharf to The Mall.
events.opNote: FREE TO WATCH but it closes a great many roads and the DLR and Jubilee line are packed all morning. Greenwich around the 10km mark is one of the best and loudest stretches.

events.name: Pride in London
events.style: Parade and stages across central London
events.typicalWhen: A Saturday in late June or early July
events.whyGo: The parade runs through the middle of town to Whitehall, and Soho - which is the reason Pride is here at all - becomes one continuous street party for the day.
events.opNote: Free. Soho is closed to traffic and rammed; Old Compton Street is the centre of it. Trafalgar Square and Golden Square hold the free stages.

events.name: Christmas at Kew
events.style: After-dark illuminated trail through the gardens
events.typicalWhen: Mid-November to early January, after dark
events.whyGo: A mile-and-a-half illuminated trail through Kew after dark, ending at the Palm House lit up and reflected in the pond - the best of London's Christmas light trails.
events.opNote: Timed entry and it sells out weeks ahead, especially at weekends. Outdoors for ninety minutes in December - dress for it properly.

events.name: The BBC Proms
events.style: Eight weeks of concerts, standing tickets from a few pounds
events.typicalWhen: Mid-July to mid-September
events.whyGo: Eight weeks of world-class orchestral music where you can stand in the arena for the price of a pint - the Promming tickets are the whole point and are sold on the day.
events.opNote: PROMMING TICKETS ARE SOLD ON THE DAY and cannot be booked - queue at the hall. Everything else books months ahead. The Last Night is balloted.

events.name: Diwali on the Square
events.style: Free Diwali celebration in Trafalgar Square
events.typicalWhen: A Sunday in October or November
events.whyGo: Free dance, music and food in Trafalgar Square for one of the largest Diwali celebrations outside India, run by the Mayor's office.
events.opNote: Free and unticketed. The date follows the lunar calendar and the nearest convenient Sunday, so it shifts between October and November.

events.name: Bonfire Night Fireworks
events.style: Firework displays across the city
events.typicalWhen: The weekend nearest 5 November
events.address: Victoria Park and parks across London
events.price: Free to ticketed depending on the park
events.whyGo: Borough displays in the big parks - Victoria Park is among the largest - on the weekend nearest the fifth of November.
events.opNote: Some borough displays are free and some now ticket to control numbers; it varies by park and changes year to year. Check the borough rather than assuming.

events.name: Greenwich Fair
events.style: Free street theatre, circus and family entertainment
events.typicalWhen: August bank holiday weekend, as part of the Greenwich+Docklands International Festival
events.address: General Wolfe Piazza, Observatory Hill, Greenwich Park
events.whyGo: Two free afternoons of street theatre, circus, puppetry and acrobatics at the top of Greenwich Park - the closing weekend of GDIF, and small enough to still feel like a local fete rather than a festival.
events.opNote: No booking - just turn up. A level access route runs from the Blackheath Gate (about 15 minutes); the step-free route from St Mary's Gate is uphill and takes 10-15 minutes.

events.name: North End Road Summer Festival
events.style: Traffic-free street festival on a Victorian market street
events.typicalWhen: A Saturday in July
events.whyGo: North End Road's market has traded six days a week since the 1880s; once a year the council closes it to traffic and adds 150-plus stalls, live music, street entertainers and free kids' workshops on top of the regular fruit-and-veg traders.
events.opNote: 10am-6pm, free, no booking. Award-winning as a community market (Best Community/Parish Market, Great British Market Awards 2019) - genuinely council-run rather than a private promotion.

events.name: Summer Sounds
events.style: Free open-air live music
events.typicalWhen: Mid-to-late August, over about ten days
events.whyGo: Ten days of free live music outdoors by the fountains at Granary Square - no ticket, no booking, and one of the better free things London puts on in August.
events.opNote: Free and unticketed, so it gets busy at the front. The canal steps behind the square are the sensible place to sit. Dates shift slightly each year.

events.name: The Classic Car Boot Sale
events.style: Vintage traders, classic cars and street food
events.venue: Granary Square, Lewis Cubitt Square and Coal Drops Yard
events.typicalWhen: Twice a year - a spring edition around April and an autumn one in September
events.address: Granary Square and Lewis Cubitt Square
events.whyGo: Over a hundred vintage traders and seventy-odd classic cars spread across three King's Cross squares, plus the UK's largest open-air Charity Super.Mkt. It passed its tenth year at King's Cross in 2025.
events.opNote: Runs 10am to 6pm across two days, and happens TWICE a year rather than once - check which edition is next before planning around it.

events.name: Wildlife Photographer of the Year
events.style: The 100 winning images from the world's biggest nature photography competition
events.typicalWhen: Mid-October to the following July
events.whyGo: The longest-running nature photography competition in the world, and consistently the Museum's strongest temporary show - 100 images chosen from tens of thousands of entries, with the conservation story behind each one.
events.opNote: Between editions as of this run - the 2025/26 exhibition closed 12 July 2026 and the next opens in October 2026. Check nhm.ac.uk before planning a visit around it specifically.
